items.title: Star Wars Nabs Spider-Man Director Jon Watts for First Movie in Disney's New Skywalker Saga Trilogy
items.description: Disney has reportedly picked Spider-Man director Jon Watts to helm the first movie in Simon Kinberg's new Star Wars trilogy as it plots out the next chapter in the Skywalker Saga.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Disney has reportedly picked Spider-Man director Jon Watts to helm the first movie in Simon Kinberg's new Star Wars trilogy as it plots out the next chapter in the Skywalker Saga.

Information about a new series of Star Wars projects from Lucasfilm was first reported by Daniel Richtman and later corroborated by The Hollywood Reporter. Although Watts is best known for leading the charge on the Marvel Cinematic Universe's Tom Holland Spider-Man trilogy, his work on Star Wars would represent his return to the sci-fi franchise following his time as co-creator on 2024's Skeleton Crew.

The yet-to-be-named new films, which are said to be the next chapter in the Skywalker Saga, are being written by Star Wars: Rebels and Mr. and Mrs. Smith veteran Kinberg. Story details remain mostly shrouded in mystery, though it's said that Daisy Ridley's sequel trilogy Jedi, Rey Skywalker, will play a role in the story.

Watts has only been picked to direct the first movie of the new trilogy so far. When this next chapter will begin is also unclear, with The Hollywood Reporter sources noting that Disney has not given the new project the official green light as work on its foundation continues.

Although still early in development, the site stated that it is further along than most other Star Wars projects. The only one ahead of it for now is Shawn Levy and Ryan Gosling's Star Wars: Starfighter, which has a May 28, 2027, release date.

Watts broke onto the blockbuster scene with the MCU's Spider-Man: Homecoming in 2017 and returned to make more superhero movies with follow-ups Far from Home and No Way Home in 2019 and 2021, respectively. He then handed over work on future Holland films to Destin Daniel Cretton, with his last feature, Wolfs, premiering in 2024.

Kinberg was first said to be in the mix to write a new Star Wars trilogy back in 2024, but there was conflicting information at the time. While some reported the next run of mainline films would continue the Skywalker Saga, others stated that the new projects would tell a completely new story. The Hollywood Reporter's story today suggested that Kinberg has settled on the former, though with the project so early in development, it's always possible that could change.

Former Lucasfilm boss Kathleen Kennedy offered an update on Kinberg's status when speaking to Deadline earlier this year. Although it seemingly ran into a few speed bumps along the way, today's update suggests the trilogy may be in the process of finding its footing and, hopefully, a path toward a full green light.

"[Kinberg] wrote something that we read in August, and it was very good, but not there," she said in January. "We've pretty much upended the story, and then spent a great deal of time on the treatment, which he finished literally about four weeks ago. And it's a very detailed treatment, like 70 pages. And so he is expected to give us something in March."

Talk to most Star Wars fans and they'll tell you the same thing: The franchise is not in the best shape at the moment – at least when it comes to its movies. The Skywalker Saga concluded a massive nine-film arc with its sequel trilogy ender, Episode 9 – The Rise of Skywalker, in 2019, but the project capped the story with more of a whimper than a bang.

Although the Ridley-led films each came with their own controversial moments, The Rise of Skywalker emerged with disappointing critical reception (IGN gave it a 7/10) rivaled only by 1999's Episode 1 – The Phantom Menace. Disney pumped the breaks when it came to theatrical releases for a galaxy far, far away after that, with this year's The Mandalorian and Grogu bringing an end to a seven-year drought without new Star Wars movies. Even that project found its own trials to overcome, with so-so critical reception (IGN's review delivered a 5/10) and underwhelming box office returns leading Disney to deem it a disappointment in theaters.

It's not all been doom and gloom for Star Wars, though. While the movies have, for many, struggled to recapture the magic of George Lucas' original vision, some of its TV outings have managed to keep audiences coming back for more. Seasons 1 and 2 of Disney's Rogue One prequel, Andor, earned the franchise critical acclaim. Meanwhile, although not everyone was sold on 2024's The Acolyte, shows like Maul – Shadow Lord and Skeleton Crew did manage to find dedicated audiences.

Star Wars is going through some growing pains as leadership shifts behind the scenes, but Disney has made it clear it still has plenty of stories to tell. There are plenty of other movies and shows in various forms of development, including Maul – Shadow Lord Season 2 and Ahsoka Season 2, which are both expected to premiere next year. While fans are still campaigning to see Adam Driver reprise his role as Kylo Ren in the canceled Hunt for Ben Solo film, Lucasfilm head Dave Filoni has signaled a bright future ahead when it comes to Star Wars movies.

Photo by Emma McIntyre/Getty Images.

items.title: Microsoft CEO Says 'Streamlining' at Xbox is 'Great to See' as Layoffs Affect Thousands
items.description: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has spoken about the state of Xbox following layoffs that affected thousands of workers, saying that the "streamlining" at the company is "great to see."
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has spoken about the state of Xbox following layoffs that affected thousands of workers, saying that the "streamlining" at the company is "great to see."

The tech executive opened up about how the business' gaming branch is doing during a recent interview on the Sources Podcast with Alex Heath. It's a conversation that followed not only the 1,600 job cuts Xbox delivered in July of this year but also the additional structural changes that were announced just this past week.

When touching on Xbox's place under the grander Microsoft umbrella, Nadella said he feels "fantastic" about the IP the brand has in its portfolio and its "ability to take that and produce great games going forward." As layoffs continue to reshape the developers who have made some of those great games, he still seems to be feeling pretty good.

"There's a certain amount of streamlining the team is doing and [Xbox CEO Asha Sharma] is doing, which is great to see," Nadella said in the wake of the most recent cuts. "And then, we have to invent the right sustainable business model that allows us to deliver gaming to more and more people.

"That has always been the goal, which is, we want to be a great publisher and a great platform provider for games across both PCs and Xboxes. So, that is our goal, and I think Asha and team have said that Xbox is going to get back to growth this next fiscal year, and that's the plan they're executing on, and in that process, do a bang-up job of producing some great games."

It's optimism that may come as a shock to those who have watched as Microsoft continues to redefine what the Xbox name means by shedding game developers like Double Fine and Ninja Theory and reorganizing beloved studios like id Software. Maybe the most telling sign that the company is entering a new chapter arrived just this past week, when it announced that Halo would be moved from Halo Studios to its Activision teams.

Xbox announced in July that it could be laying off 1,600 staff, with an additional 1,600 set to follow before the end of the fiscal year. Although this past week offered a closer look at what that long-term plan entails, we won't know the full scope of the company's big "reset" initiative for at least a few more months.

For now, the resulting changes also include the Fallout: New Vegas team at Obsidian Entertainment moving under Bethesda. After State of Decay developer Undead Labs confirmed its independence just days ago, studio head Philip Holt told IGN that the zombie series' third game remains in active development amid its own "significant" wave of layoffs.

For more on how the industry has changed in recent months, you can read about what Nadella had to say about how Xbox's monetization plan at Microsoft compares to YouTube. You can also catch up on what he said about the brand when former Xbox CEO Phil Spencer departed the company.

Photo by George Chan/Getty Images.

items.title: Discord Users are Massacring Wumpus in Increasingly Gruesome Ways to Protest Platform's Age Verification System
items.description: Discord artists are tearing the company's purple mascot, Wumpus, limb from limb in increasingly gruesome ways to protest its controversial age verification system.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Discord artists are tearing the company's purple mascot, Wumpus, limb from limb in increasingly gruesome ways to protest its controversial age verification system.

Despite the backlash already surrounding Discord's new system, its launch started innocently enough. Then, when the company took to X/Twitter to sarcastically refer to the changes as "extremely popular" amid early bugs, fans unleashed hell on the cutesy purple avatar.

when you launch an extremely popular age assurance update that everyone on Discord was really looking forward to and it has bugs https://t.co/I9dVu9ZhET pic.twitter.com/BLAz9fWTSn

— Discord (@discord) September 24, 2026

"When you launch an extremely popular age assurance update that everyone on Discord was really looking forward to and it has bugs," Discord said.

The post in question was posted earlier this week and has 36K likes, but the nearly 10K replies already signal that not all is well amongst users. Open up the quotes for the post, and you'll be met with what feels like an endless sea of fan art featuring none other than Discord's plum mascot, Wumpus. These days, he's looking more red than purple, though.

The top post quoting the original message is accompanied by no text. Instead, it features a hyper-realistic version of Wumpus being subjected to a form of torture called "quartering," which sees an individual pulled into pieces by horses tied to each of their limbs.

This post alone has 260K likes. It is far from the only image of its kind.

https://t.co/tiscKCgzOj pic.twitter.com/teeA9k8vS0

— fishman (@asianfissureman) September 25, 2026

“Extremely popular” pic.twitter.com/vq9Ke1seg9

— radionerd (@radionerdxbox) September 25, 2026

I will never be a memory, Wumpus. https://t.co/ZcXfKG1e1T pic.twitter.com/t58VixRwmv

— Capidol 🍀|| C0mms OPEN (@CapidolArt) September 26, 2026

pic.twitter.com/MoamXpthQT

— Conor D. Oil (@RealConorOil) September 24, 2026

Whether he's facing eldritch horrors, Broly, Sephiroth's Masamune, or packs of wolves, Wumpus is going through it. Everyone online is having a great time watching the leaf-wearing avatar get torn to shreds, but they've also made it clear that the violence being unleashed upon him isn't coming from a positive place.

It's all in response to Discord's age verification system, which has faced its own onslaught of backlash since it was first announced earlier this year. As the platform has been reminded today, many of its millions of users have been vocal when it comes to privacy concerns following a significant data breach just last year.

"If you want to be a serious grown-up data stealing company you can’t smol bean post anymore," one user said in response to Discord's post.

"Stop trying to quirk chungus your data harvesting scheme," another said. "We cannot stand your ass."

lol https://t.co/T5DLuzxjdQ pic.twitter.com/Sdvb8jXmcN

— Junjou Laina 🔥 GIGGINOX 4 ASCENDANCE 🔥 (@Jun_on_Fire) September 26, 2026

"'Extremely popular age assurance update.' Are we f**kin serious," another user asked.

"No we are so fckin sarcastic," Discord replied.

Shortly after Wumpus was (quite literally) thrown into the line of fire, Discord posted an update saying that bugs blocking age-restricted servers had been fixed. The company has not addressed the criticisms filling its replies section since the new system went live.

items.title: The Last of Us Gets Animated Background on PS5 as Naughty Dog Teases Announcements for TLOU Day 2026
items.description: Naughty Dog has released a free background on PlayStation 5 as it prepares to celebrate The Last of Us Day 2026.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Naughty Dog has released a free background on PlayStation 5 as it prepares to celebrate The Last of Us Day 2026.

The studio behind Sony's exclusive post-apocalyptic video game franchise took to social media to tease some of what it has planned for this year's festivities. While September 26 is technically the day it's chosen to serve as its Cordyceps-breakout holiday, Naughty Dog won't share any The Last of Us announcements with fans until Monday the 28th, but that doesn't mean there's nothing to fawn over today.

PS5 owners can now head to their consoles to download a special The Last of Us-themed background for PlayStation's Welcome Hub landing page. It's a free option featuring both the younger and older versions of Ellie from both mainline games, with no download required to enjoy it. Although it's far from the kind of dynamic themes or wallpapers fans have begged Sony to bring back, the animated background does add some flavor for fans still hoping to see the series get a proper return in games.

We'll be celebrating #TLOUDay on Monday, but we do have a fun surprise for you today. 🧡🩵

For the first time ever, a The Last of Us-themed background is being added to the PlayStation Welcome Hub. Log in to your PlayStation account and download it to see how our team has… pic.twitter.com/aK6F85FM2I

— Naughty Dog (@Naughty_Dog) September 26, 2026

Those who want to spice up their PS5 backgrounds need only to navigate to the Welcome Hub, select the Change Background button in the top corner of the screen, and then select The Last of Us background in the Games tab. It's nothing much, but we'll only have to wait a few more days to hear more about The Last of Us Day celebration.

In a separate post, Naughty Dog promised September 28 will bring even more reveals for the franchise. While it doesn't sound like something like The Last of Us Part 3 will be discussed, the team did promise to share a "partnership announcement, a very cool collaboration, digital surprises, and more." There will also be a No Return charity stream on Twitch.

Another surprise announced today was the news that The Last of Us Season 3 on HBO has picked up some new and familiar faces: John Goodman, Laura Bailey, and Ian Alexander. Goodman, a series newcomer and award-winning actor, will play a new character named Joey. Bailey, who played Abby in The Last of Us Part 2 and a nurse in The Last of Us Season 1, will play a Seraphite leader named Elizabeth, while Alexander will play a currently unnamed character after first appearing as Lev in the second game.

We'll have to wait to see what Naughty Dog has planned for The Last of Us Day 2026. While Sony has yet to confirm a The Last of Us Part 3 as work on its Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet continues, fans are hoping an announcement will arrive sooner rather than later. One comment from creator Neil Druckmann sparked theories about a third chapter in Ellie's story in March of this year.

items.title: Minecraft Confirms Ice Caves as Next Game Drop, Adds Frozen Zombies, Ice Balls, and More
items.description: Mojang has teased Minecraft’s next game drop, giving fans a sneak peek at some of its features.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Mojang has teased Minecraft’s next game drop, giving fans a sneak peek at some of its features.

As revealed at Minecraft LIVE, Ice Caves are coming to the game, adding a new and rare underground extension of cold biomes with glowing ice crystals and environmental variety. Ice Caves include a new hostile mob, the frozen zombie, which can apply freezing effects and throw damaging ice balls. The ice balls can also be used as weapons or to craft potions, adding strategic options for combat scenarios.

Mojang said Ice Caves add a whole new layer of variety to cold biomes, making exploring underground even more interesting, thanks to the increased environmental diversity. “Though they may be beautiful, these caves are far from safe,” the developer said.

Ice crystals can be found in ice caves and can be placed both vertically and horizontally, providing lots of potential for decoration and building. They can even be used as a light source. The Frozen Zombie, meanwhile, applies a stacking freezing effect with its melee attacks. If you take enough hits, you'll freeze. It also throws ice balls at you, which apply knockback and deal damage. Normal zombies can convert into Frozen when exposed to powder snow. Players can already convert Husks into Zombies, and now Zombies into Frozen, opening the door for advanced mob farms.

Frozen drop ice balls on death, allowing players to use them as well, but they can also be crafted and used to brew a new potion. As a weapon, ice balls deal damage and apply knockback, and as a potion it can freeze players.

For more, check out everything announced at Minecraft LIVE.

items.description: Minecraft World got two announcements at Minecraft LIVE today: the world’s first official Minecraft hotel, and the name of the first ever Minecraft rollercoaster.

items.content:
Minecraft World got two announcements at Minecraft LIVE today: the world’s first official Minecraft hotel, and the name of the first ever Minecraft rollercoaster.

Minecraft World Hotel and the Escape the Nether rollercoaster are confirmed for the Minecraft experience at Chessington World of Adventures Resort, and are set to open their doors at some point next year, Merlin Entertainments and Mojang Studios announced.

Check out all the new Minecraft World images and photos in the slideshow below.

Concept art already released for Minecraft World features wooden houses, Creepers, TNT blocks, and even a Nether dining area. Expect interactive adventures, blockbuilt playscapes, and themed retail.

For more, check out everything announced at Minecraft LIVE.

items.title: Minecraft Is Getting Its First New Dimension in Over 14 Years
items.description: Minecraft developer Mojang has announced that the Sift is coming to Java and Bedrock Edition in 2027 — the game's first new dimension in over 14 years.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Minecraft developer Mojang has announced that the Sift is coming to Java and Bedrock Edition in 2027 — the game's first new dimension in over 14 years.

As revealed at Minecraft LIVE September 2026, the Sift, which had been announced for upcoming dungeon crawler Minecraft Dungeons 2, is also coming to Minecraft Java and Bedrock Edition next year. It joins the Overworld, The Nether, and The End as Minecraft’s official fourth dimension.

Today at Minecraft LIVE: Dungeons II, our first new dimension in more than 14 years, new ways for creators to build, Minecraft on Nintendo Switch 2, and more.

More than 300,000 people play Minecraft for the first time on an average day. After 17+ years and 425M+ copies sold, I… pic.twitter.com/fdhkwuh258

— ASHA (@asha_shar) September 26, 2026

Mojang said next to nothing about the Sift in terms of how it will work in vanilla during Minecraft LIVE, and only teased how it will look during the stream. Here's Mojang's official blurb on the Sift, which briefly touched on the new mob which we can see in the image above.

Minecraft LIVE revealed that the newest Minecraft dimension isn’t just finding its home in Dungeons II, it’ll also be coming to Minecraft Java & Bedrock Edition next year. This will be the first new dimension in over 14 years – joining the Overworld, the Nether and the End as our fourth dimension. During the broadcast, you got a glimpse into this dimension in Minecraft – and even one of the mobs that calls it home. But surely that’s not enough! Luckily you can experience it for yourself in Minecraft Dungeons II – coming September 29, 2026.

Perhaps we should look to the Sift in Minecraft Dungeons 2 to get a sense of what to expect. In the dungeon crawler, the Sift is described as "beautiful, vibrant, and teeming with souls." It features new biomes such as the Meadow and the Carapace.

For more, check out everything announced at Minecraft LIVE.

items.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Extended Clip Reveals Closer Look at Ganondorf
items.description: Nintendo has published a short clip that shows a closer look at Ganondorf in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Nintendo has published a short clip that shows a closer look at Ganondorf in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.

Those who have the Nintendo Today! app downloaded on their mobile devices were treated to more footage from the upcoming reimagining yesterday. The video in question is, crushingly, only 16 seconds long, but it reveals an extended look at how The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is reincarnating one of video games' most iconic villains for Nintendo Switch 2.

"A man from the Gerudo, a tribe in which men are said to be born only once in a hundred years," official text shared by Nintendo said. "He harbors a grand ambition to obtain the Triforce, a sacred relic rumored to grant the wish of any individual who touches it."

GANONDORF IN THE NEW SNEAK PEAK FOR OCARINA OF TIME??? holy shit he's so cool pic.twitter.com/Q85Im9XA6Y

— bea (@SlLENTPRINCESS) September 25, 2026

We first saw how Ganondorf would fit into the remake's divisive art style when Nintendo unveiled gameplay during its dedicated Direct earlier this month. The new footage expands on the updated dream sequence shown previously, showing the evildoer riding on horseback as voiceover says, "And now… An evil has appeared, yearning after that power."

While technically a scene players have already been looking at for decades, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake will alter the moment with more than just shiny new graphics, even if the changes are small. As highlighted in the Nintendo Today! post, while the extended clip shows that the Switch 2 version of the scene is running in slow motion, the original Nintendo 64 and 3DS remake versions show Ganondorf moving like normal.

Again, it's an extremely small change, but it's also yet another sign that the November reimagining will come with a few tweaks to a classic that fans may want to prepare themselves for. It all arrives as fans continue to be torn about some of the promised tweaks, just as a dedicated jump button, while Nintendo chose to intentionally retain the loading screens from the original experience.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake launches for Switch 2 November 5, 2026. For more, you can read about the time Ubisoft reportedly scrapped a Zelda spinoff with Ganondorf as the protagonist. You can also learn about how Shigeru Miyamoto's love for puppetry may have influenced the remake's art style.

items.title: Melissa Barrera Says She Would Reprise Her Scream Role, Reveals Conditions for Her Return
items.description: Actress Melissa Barrera said she is open to returning to Scream, but don't expect to see her reprise her role as Sam Carpenter as long as Spyglass Media has the rights.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Actress Melissa Barrera said she is open to returning to Scream, but don't expect to see her reprise her role as Sam Carpenter as long as Spyglass Media has the rights.

The Scream 5 and Scream 6 star opened up about what it would take to bring her back to Wes Craven's legendary slasher franchise during an interview with JustWatch. Barrera explained that she still "loves the franchise," but the people overseeing it are what's keeping her from going another round with Ghostface.

"Not with the company that currently holds the rights," she said when asked if she would return if she got a call to reprise her role. "I love the franchise. I had an amazing time making those movies, but a lot of the hate and difficulty that I've faced in the last years is because the leadership of that company made it a point to label me something that I'm not."

"And they never apologized, even when I was proven right. Even with an apology, I wouldn't go back to work with them – not that I'm holding my breath. I don't think they have that ability."

Barrera starred in two installments for the horror franchise and was set to return for a third run with Jenna Ortega but was fired by Spyglass following a series of pro-Palestine social media posts she published in late 2023. At the time, Spyglass said it has "zero tolerance for antisemitism or the incitement of hate."

"I pray day and night for no more deaths, for no more violence, and for peaceful co-existence," Barrera said in a statement following her firing. "I will continue to speak out for those that need it most and continue to advocate for peace and safety, for human rights and freedom. Silence is not an option for me."

The Scream rights holder's move was immediately met with backlash from fans for more reasons than one. Barrera had helped bring the franchise back to theaters after a decade without a new installment, and when she was unceremoniously removed as the lead of Scream 7, other talent happened to follow suit. Jenna Ortega departed Scream 7 just weeks after it all went down. Director Christopher Landon confirmed his exit just one month after Spyglass fired Barrera.

Paramount Pictures and Spyglass went on to release a very different vision for the franchise when Scream 7 premiered earlier this year. Although familiar faces helped it break records at the box office, the latest entry debuted to franchise-low reviews, as shared by Rotten Tomatoes. IGN gave it a 6/10. Scream 8 is also reportedly in the works.

Despite veering off in a completely new direction, Barrera said now that she's open to coming back. For her, it's not just about working under new management but honoring Craven's legacy.

"If the franchise were ever to leave those hands and go into hands that would, I think, honor Wes Craven's legacy more… I think, yeah," she continued regarding her interest in a return to the franchise.

For now, Barrera remains uninvolved with Scream. Series star Matthew Lillard recently spoke up about his surprise return in Scream 7. During a recent Q&A (via Deadline), he said he was "embarrassed" to have reprised his role.

" I’m just gonna say, what happened to Melissa, the whole world didn’t pipe up," he said. "She was like a year early on what the f**k’s going on, but the whole world should have piped up and said, ‘she’s right,’ and they didn’t. And that’s brutal."

For now, Scream 8 has no release date. Although ideas for the next film are something that have been in the works behind the scenes for some time, there's no information about who may show up in it.

items.title: New Werwulf Trailer and Tie-In Video Game Revealed
items.description: Focus Features has released the new official trailer for Robert Eggers’ Werwulf, alongside a surprise video game reveal for the medieval horror film.
items.author: Jim Vejvoda
items.content:
Focus Features is releasing all its major marketing and asset reveals for director Robert Eggers’ Werwulf according to the calendar of the full moon. That’s why the new trailer for the medieval horror film dropped today.

Werwulf follows a 13th-century farmer (Aaron Taylor-Johnson), who is cursed to live as a werewolf. Lily-Rose Depp plays his wife and the mother of his children, while Willem Dafoe, Ralph Ineson, and Jack Morris play a trio of wolf hunters on a mission to kill the werewolf.

You can watch the new trailer below.

In addition to the trailer, Focus also announced the Werwulf Alternate Reality Game today.

The game is timed to each of the full moons between September through November 2026 and, according to what Focus revealed, “culminates in a mysterious prize for those that complete all three moons each full moon.”

Players can visit DevourethAllMankynde.com where they need “to seek out a hidden ‘sign’ on various digital platforms and decipher the sign back into the site in order to fulfill the moon. The catch is, you only get 24 hours each full moon to search for the sign before it disappears so you’ll need to work fast to find it.” The first clue can be found here.

For more on Werwulf, discover the latest details Robert Eggers revealed about his “Hell-like” medieval horror film.

Werwulf opens in cinemas on December 25.

items.title: John Goodman, Laura Bailey, and Ian Alexander to Star in HBO's The Last of Us Season 3
items.description: Emmy-winning actor John Goodman, prolific voice talent Laura Bailey, and returning star Ian Alexander have been cast in the third (and possibly final) season of HBO’s The Last of Us series.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Emmy-winning actor John Goodman, prolific voice talent Laura Bailey, and returning star Ian Alexander have been cast in the third (and possibly final) season of HBO’s The Last of Us series.

As revealed on September 26 — the day the Cordyceps infection ravaged humanity in The Last of Us universe — the show’s third season will feature three big talents, two of whom are making their return to Naughty Dog’s flagship zombie franchise.

Perhaps most surprisingly, John Goodman has been slated to play a character named Joey, a figure who wasn’t in the original games. Joey is joined by another character named Paco, who will be played by Ian Alexander; the two are described as a “friendly duo who dub themselves ‘Heroes of the Highway.’” Alexander notably played Lev in The Last of Us Part 2, a young boy who Abby helps rescue from the Seraphite cult.

The Seraphites will play a part in season 3, as Laura Bailey is set to play Elizabeth, one of the cult’s leaders. Bailey is also a returning actor to the franchise, having famously voiced Abby in The Last of Us Part 2 alongside Alexander.

With the Seraphites being included in the third season and Alexander playing a new character, it stands to reason that another person will be playing Lev, most likely because Alexander has aged out of the role.

These two aren’t the only actors from the original games who have been included in HBO’s screen adaptation; Ashley Johnson and Troy Baker also played characters in The Last of Us Season 1, with Johnson playing Ellie’s mother in a harrowing birth scene and Baker playing James, a member of Baker’s villainous group.

Johnson and Baker famously provided the voice and motion performances for Ellie and Joel in both of The Last of Us Games, so it’s not surprising that Bailey and Alexander are also showing up in some way.

HBO’s The Last of Us series is expected to end with this forthcoming season, which will air in 2027. In a September interview with Deadline, the Chairman and CEO of HBO and Max Content, Casey Bloys, said he “thinks [showrunner] Craig [Mazin] has planned it as the final season.”

Bloys has been hinting at this since January, saying in another Deadline interview that “it certainly seems that way, but on decisions like that, we will defer to the showrunners. So you can ask them.”

With the games’ creator, Niel Druckmann, having left the project after Season 2, the future of HBO’s show is looking uncertain — but with talent like Alexander, Bailey, and Goodman on board, there’s bound to be some fantastic performances in store. We just hope they don’t tear our hearts apart like Nick Offerman did in the first season.

Image Credits: Henry NICHOLLS / AFP via Getty Images

items.title: Werwulf Director Robert Eggers Reveals New Details About His 'Hell-Like' Medieval Horror Film
items.description: Director Robert Eggers reveals eerie new details about Werwulf, his upcoming medieval horror film starring Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Willem Dafoe and Lily-Rose Depp.
items.author: Jim Vejvoda
items.content:
“After Nosferatu, I kind of said, ‘Let me try to write the scariest thing I can write.’ I don't know that I did that, but I definitely wrote the darkest thing,” writer-director Robert Eggers told the press at a promotional event Friday for his upcoming horror film, Werwulf. And based on the roughly 20 minutes of select footage I saw from the film, Werwulf indeed has all the makings of being Eggers’ darkest and scariest movie yet.

Werwulf follows a 13th-century farmer (Aaron Taylor-Johnson), simply referred to as Man, who is cursed as a werewolf. Lily-Rose Depp plays his wife and the mother of his children, while Willem Dafoe, Ralph Ineson, and Jack Morris play a trio of wolf hunters on a mission to kill the werewolf.

Eggers kicked the event off by screening the opening scene of Werwulf, a dialogue-free nighttime sequence. The howling of wolves can be heard over a black screen. Then the Man’s face is revealed. He is foaming at the mouth and in great pain. The Man sprints naked through the woods and enters an empty home. Inside, he suffers wild convulsions in the moonlight and growls in agony. He writhes on the floor, and eventually ends up in the shadows where his transformation continues unseen. Taylor-Johnson performed all these body-bending movements himself (save for one shot that could not be accomplished practically), and it was truly a wild sight to behold. Eggers stressed, though, “that is not the set piece werewolf transformation.”

“I think werewolf movies are a difficult genre. And I think sometimes even if it's a great werewolf movie, it's hard to believe that your dad's turning into a werewolf or your next door neighbor who's a high school basketball player is turning into a werewolf,” Eggers said. But a period werewolf movie “really helps ground you and ground the audience. At least that's the intention.”

While I won’t give blow-by-blow details of the other scenes in order to avoid spoilers, the additional footage showed: aspects of the Man’s youth; hints at how and why he ended up cursed; the arrival of three wolf hunters at the Man’s home in the middle of the night to violently enlist his help in hunting down a werewolf; and the Man and the hunters’ journey to find a strange old woman who may know a thing or two about werewolves.

"It was designed to be kind of like a silent movie.

Eggers did copious amounts of research on England in the 13th century for the screenplay, he co-wrote with his The Northman collaborator, Sjón. The film’s dialogue is in Middle English, although it’s been altered by dialect coach William Conacher to make it more comprehensible for the modern ear. Eggers also worked with two Middle English scholars at Oxford University, Eleanor Baker and Daniel Wakelin, who helped make the dialogue more period accurate.

Although the dialogue is in Middle English, Eggers said that Werwulf “was designed to be kind of like a silent movie. You don't need to understand what anyone's saying to understand the movie because you're with everyone on an emotional level, particularly Aaron and his family.”

Eggers’ fascination with werewolf lore goes back to this youth. “The historical werewolves that I had read about starting in high school, they were doing things that were so taboo and hard for anyone to wrap their mind around because it was so extreme that the culture that they existed in said, ‘You can't be a human, you must be a werewolf.’ So it was going to be very dark and very primal subject matter,” the filmmaker said.

“I wanted to make it in England and because Edward I was trying to protect the wool trade around the time of this movie, he set a campaign to exterminate all the wolves. Actually, Willem's character is based on a real person who did such a good job that in another 200 years there were not wolves in England. So without wolves, you don't have werewolf lore. So if I was going to set it in England, it had to be this early in history around 1300. And that was even more exciting, because the world would be so primitive and so visceral and primal that that would make this all the more dark and brutal.”

"’Does this take place in hell?

The world of Werwulf is so dark and brutal that Eggers’ said cinematographer Jarin Blaschke texted him after he first read the script and asked, "’Does this take place in hell?’ And it needs to be hell for Aaron. And I think some medievalists would be annoyed that I'm kind of clinging to the stereotype of the Middle Ages being so muddy and dirty and rainy and miserable, but it needs to be so muddy, and rainy, and dirty, and miserable, and shit-covered, and it does need to be hell. But again, I always find that doing the research about the period, you learn stuff that makes it more interesting and more specific. And for this particular movie, more hell-like.”

Audiences will discover for themselves just how hell-like Werwulf is when it opens in theaters Christmas Day.

Eggers stressed, though, “that is not the set piece werewolf transformation.”

“I think werewolf movies are a difficult genre. And I think sometimes even if it's a great werewolf movie, it's hard to believe that your dad's turning into a werewolf or your next door neighbor who's a high school basketball player is turning into a werewolf,” Eggers said. But a period werewolf movie “really helps ground you and ground the audience. At least that's the intention.”

While I won’t give blow-by-blow details of the other scenes in order to avoid spoilers, the additional footage showed: aspects of the Man’s youth; hints at how and why he ended up cursed; the arrival of three wolf hunters at the Man’s home in the middle of the night to violently enlist his help in hunting down a werewolf; and the Man and the hunters’ journey to find a strange old woman who may know a thing or two about werewolves.

"It was designed to be kind of like a silent movie.

Eggers did copious amounts of research on England in the 13th century for the screenplay, he co-wrote with his The Northman collaborator, Sjón. The film’s dialogue is in Middle English, although it’s been altered by dialect coach William Conacher to make it more comprehensible for the modern ear. Eggers also worked with two Middle English scholars at Oxford University, Eleanor Baker and Daniel Wakelin, who helped make the dialogue more period accurate.

Although the dialogue is in Middle English, Eggers said that Werwulf “was designed to be kind of like a silent movie. You don't need to understand what anyone's saying to understand the movie because you're with everyone on an emotional level, particularly Aaron and his family.”

Eggers’ fascination with werewolf lore goes back to this youth. “The historical werewolves that I had read about starting in high school, they were doing things that were so taboo and hard for anyone to wrap their mind around because it was so extreme that the culture that they existed in said, ‘You can't be a human, you must be a werewolf.’ So it was going to be very dark and very primal subject matter,” the filmmaker said.

“I wanted to make it in England and because Edward I was trying to protect the wool trade around the time of this movie, he set a campaign to exterminate all the wolves. So if I was going to set it in England, it had to be this early in history around 1300. And that was even more exciting, because the world would be so primitive and so visceral and primal that that would make this all the more dark and brutal.”

"’Does this take place in hell?

The world of Werwulf is so dark and brutal that Eggers’ said cinematographer Jarin Blaschke texted him after he first read the script and asked, "’Does this take place in hell?’ And it needs to be hell for Aaron. And I think some medievalists would be annoyed that I'm kind of clinging to the stereotype of the Middle Ages being so muddy and dirty and rainy and miserable, but it needs to be so muddy, and rainy, and dirty, and miserable, and shit-covered, and it does need to be hell. But again, I always find that doing the research about the period, you learn stuff that makes it more interesting and more specific. And for this particular movie, more hell-like.”

Audiences will discover for themselves just how hell-like Werwulf is when it opens in theaters Christmas Day.

items.title: Minecraft LIVE September 2026 — Everything Announced
items.description: Minecraft LIVE wrapped up with a number of big announcements for the game. We've got everything you need to know right here.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Minecraft LIVE September 2026 featured a number of big announcements for the game, which we've rounded up below.

The headline announcement was confirmation that the Sift is coming to Minecraft Java and Bedrock Edition in 2027. It's the first new dimension for Minecraft in 14 years. Elsewhere, Mojang confirmed that Ice Caves are the next game drop, and Sound Effects Packs for Minecraft Marketplace are coming later this year. We also got an update on Minecraft World, which is getting a hotel and a rollercoaster.

Alas, there was no announcement of an End update, as some fans had speculated might have been on the way. I guess those Enderman teases in the Minecraft LIVE trailer weren't teases after all!

All this and more is detailed in the report below. Check that out, then head to the comments to let us know what you think!

And that's a wrap!

Minecraft LIVE is over, and we have a clearer idea of what's coming to Minecraft for the rest of this year and even 2027. Let us know what you thought of all the announcements in the comments!

The Sift is coming to Java and Bedrock Edition!

Minecraft LIVE's big final announcement is that the Sift is coming to Minecraft Java and Bedrock Edition in 2027. The Sift is Minecraft's first new dimension in over 14 years, and joins the Overworld, The Nether, and The End as Minecraft’s official fourth dimension.

Today at Minecraft LIVE: Dungeons II, our first new dimension in more than 14 years, new ways for creators to build, Minecraft on Nintendo Switch 2, and more.

More than 300,000 people play Minecraft for the first time on an average day. After 17+ years and 425M+ copies sold, I… pic.twitter.com/fdhkwuh258

— ASHA (@asha_shar) September 26, 2026

Ice Caves are the next Minecraft game drop

Ice Caves are coming to Minecraft, adding a new and rare underground extension of cold biomes with glowing ice crystals and environmental variety. Ice Caves include a new hostile mob, the frozen zombie, which can apply freezing effects and throw damaging ice balls. The ice balls can also be used as weapons or to craft potions, adding strategic options for combat scenarios.

Mojang said Ice Caves add a whole new layer of variety to cold biomes, making exploring underground even more interesting, thanks to the increased environmental diversity. “Though they may be beautiful, these caves are far from safe,” the developer said.

Ice crystals can be found in ice caves and can be placed both vertically and horizontally, providing lots of potential for decoration and building. They can even be used as a light source. The Frozen Zombie, meanwhile, applies a stacking freezing effect with its melee attacks. If you take enough hits, you'll freeze. It also throws ice balls at you, which apply knockback and deal damage. Normal zombies can convert into Frozen when exposed to powder snow. Players can already convert Husks into Zombies, and now Zombies into Frozen, opening the door for advanced mob farms.

Frozen drop ice balls on death, allowing players to use them as well, but they can also be crafted and used to brew a new potion. As a weapon, ice balls deal damage and apply knockback, and as a potion it can freeze players.

Sound Effects Packs for Minecraft Marketplace coming later this year

Later this year Mojang will introduce Sound Effects Packs for Minecraft Marketplace, giving players new ways to customize their experience.

Minecraft World update

Minecraft World got two announcements at Minecraft LIVE today: the world’s first official Minecraft hotel, and the name of the first ever Minecraft rollercoaster.

Minecraft World Hotel and the Escape the Nether rollercoaster are confirmed for the Minecraft experience at Chessington World of Adventures Resort, and are set to open their doors at some point next year, Merlin Entertainments and Mojang Studios announced.

Minecraft Dungeons 2 deep dive

Mojang showed off more of Minecraft Dungeons 2, as expected. Expect plenty of loot, mobs, and a new dimension. Story wise, you have to help the villages find a new home in the town of Bravehaven. When you start to explore outside the town you realize there's a soul corruption happening in the overworld.

The world is interconnected this time, so it's more open for you to take your own route with a freedom to explore. You get to know the Villagers better in this game, helping them out as a player. And you can jump! There are small parkour sections to find secrets and even jump attacks.

The big hook here is the Sift, a brand new dimension in Minecraft Dungeons 2. It's an environment rich with souls. Expect DLC post-launch, too. Minecraft Dungeons 2 launches this Tuesday, September 29.

Brave a new dimension in #DungeonsII: The Sift!

Hear what our team has to say about this beautiful new world. pic.twitter.com/EWfVrHL2JD

— Minecraft (@Minecraft) September 26, 2026

New Minecraft platform initiative

Minecraft LIVE began with Jens Bergenström, Chief Creative Officer at Mojang Studios, ruling out an End update. Bah! He did, however, announce a new creator platform designed to get more people creating experiences within Minecraft. It's all pretty vague, but it sounds like Mojang is thinking about taking on Roblox by making it easier to build experiences within Minecraft. We'll hopefully have more on how this all works soon.

30 minutes to go!

This is your official 30 minute warning for Minecraft LIVE! Not long now until we find out what Mojang has up its sleeve. Check back here for live updates, and let us know what you're hoping to see in the comments!

items.title: Marvel's Wolverine Dev Adds Option to Turn Off Controversial Scent Trails and More in New Update
items.description: Insomniac Games has published a new Marvel's Wolverine update that adds an option to turn off those controversial scent trails for collectibles.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Insomniac Games has published a new Marvel's Wolverine update that adds an option to turn off those controversial scent trails for collectibles.

The Sony developer made good on its promise to investigate a proper on/off option when version 1.001.006 launched just hours ago. Its patch notes reveal more targeted changes as the studio works out the remaining kinks that have emerged in the days since Marvel's Wolverine launched for PlayStation 5.

There are three new toggle settings that players can now use to customize their gameplay experience: one for Whiskey Bottle scent trails, one for Material Crate Audio Clues, and one for Nightmare Door Roots. Those first two proved to be an especially hot topic online, with players criticizing in-game hints as one of a few examples of a game many feel is too 'hand-holdy.' Adding the option to completely turn these guides off should quiet those concerns, with a toggle for Nightmare Door Roots adding even more freedom for players to tailor their Marvel's Wolverine experience to their liking.

The new toggles are pretty straightforward. If players find the wavy visuals to be a bit too distracting, they can simply turn them off. As noted in the in-game settings, using Wolverine's Crate Finder and Whiskey Finder Adaptations will override any flipped toggles.

The update also tackles some crashes reported by the community, as well as a few pesky glitches. For example, one of the more common problems fans may have seen in viral clips online was Logan getting his claws stuck when sliding down an early-game tree. Insomniac said that should be fixed now, with an issue tied to misaligned claws in photo mode fixed, too.

Another squashed bug outlined in the patch notes involves some strange bathroom signs. Players feared the signs suggested Insomniac had used generative AI in Marvel's Wolverine before the studio stepped in to deny the accusations with an explanation. They won't be an eyesore going forward.

Instead of fans spending their time talking about the new Wolverine game's mutant-filled story or its bloody action, the conversation surrounding the launch of the new PS5 exclusive mostly revolved around things like scent trails for collectibles, a motorcycle chase sequence, and 'fart gas.' Although the new update can make it more difficult to search for and find Whiskey Bottles and Material Crates, story-driven scent trails and senses – like the one that allows Logan to track Jean in The One That Got Away mission – will remain regardless of toggled settings.

On that front, Insomniac has taken measures to make story scent trails a bit less intrusive. Last week's update reduced trail opacity, effectively nerfing the so-called fart gas without completely removing it from the experience.

Marvel's Wolverine launched for PS5 September 15, 2026. In the wake of controversy surrounding certain mechanics and features, Insomniac said it would keep its ear to the ground when it came to community feedback. It's a message studio director of community and marketing James Stevenson repeated following the new update.

"As I have said we continue to listen and work with the team to address feedback and requests," he said on X/Twitter.

Marvel’s Wolverine is out now exclusively on the PlayStation 5. You can read our review of the game here, or peep our 17 Essential Tips and Tricks to help you get started in Marvel’s Wolverine, plus our recommendations for the 10 Best Adaptations, and a guide on How to Farm XP Quickly. Check out our full Marvel’s Wolverine Walkthrough for a step-by-step guide to every mission, and make sure you don’t miss a thing with our Collectibles guides for Whisky Bottle locations to help boost your Adaptations and Weapons Crate locations that help you unlock all Wolverine Suits and Claws, and our thorough list of all the Easter Eggs and References we've found. Oh, and it's only 20 hours to a Platinum Trophy according to our reviewer, here's a guide to that!

Marvel's Wolverine Update 1.001.006

*NEW* Update 1.001.006

This update includes Senses toggles for Whisky Bottle Scent Trails, Material Crate Audio Clues, and Nightmare Door Roots. It also addresses several community-reported crashes and bugs.

Full hotfix notes below:

  • Adds new on/off Senses toggles for*:
    • Whisky Bottle Scent Trails
    • Material Crate Audio Clues
    • Nightmare Door Roots
  • Addresses several crashes identified through crash logs & the community
  • Fixes an issue where players could become stuck while sliding down tree in the "The One That Got Away" mission
  • Addresses issues with misaligned claws in Photo Mode
  • Fixes rare issue where objects may turn white after extended play sessions
  • Fixes overlapping bathroom sign in the casino caused by a UV mapping issue

*Story-critical Senses will still appear in the world.

items.title: Chris Hansen Announces His Own Documentary After Watching 'Fever Dream' Primetime and Grades Movie a D
items.description: Chris Hansen says he was more confused than offended by Lance Oppenheim’s Primetime, and is answering this dramatized version of events with his own documentary.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Chris Hansen says he was more confused than offended by Lance Oppenheim’s Primetime, and is answering this dramatized version of events with his own documentary.

Chris Hansen has finally seen Primetime, which he watched in a Times Square theater alongside an audience of average moviegoers — and he says he was more baffled by the film than anything else.

He’s also got “a number of documentaries” about his life and career in the works, one of which is currently being shopped around to multiple different platforms.

Hansen delivered the news during an interview with fellow host and journalist Jesse Watters on his YouTube channel after watching Primetime, where he revealed the documentary’s title: I am Chris Hansen.

“It’s a project, a film, in which I cooperated, produced by folks obviously I know and work with, and it was in the works well before we even heard of Primetime,” he said. “It’s pretty good timing to have this thing out there with our agents shopping it on the West Coast to various platforms.”

Hansen went on to give his review of the movie, which he graded a D. (Hey, at least it wasn’t an F.) And while Hansen praised Robert Pattinson’s performance, he felt the actor’s portrayal of him deviated significantly from who he was as a person — to the point where it was like watching a totally different person on the screen. And that, for Hansen, makes it so separate from his own identity that it’s hard to be offended by it.

“What was in it, in my mind, was something that was so overly-dramatized, so detached from reality — as the director put it, a fever dream — that it almost hit me as something that was so far from reality that it wouldn't even bother me, and I think other filmgoers will experience the same thing.

“In a way, it's a hit piece on me and the series, which is weird, because all we do is expose bad human beings who try to hurt children. So in that respect, it's sort of an insult to the thousands of men and women who want, every day, to do the same thing that I try to do in Takedown and did in To Catch a Predator. It's so far over the top that it's hard to come to grips with what they're trying to do here.”

Hansen went on to mention a specific scene in the film where Pattinson sits in front of a vanity mirror, shirtless, rehearsing what he plans to say to the supposed predators when he gets them on camera. This, like "almost every one” of the other scenes in Primetime, “didn’t happen,” according to Hansen.

Hansen went on to reiterate that he was never approached by A24 about the film. Previously, he claimed that he’d refused to sign a waiver before entering a screening of the movie, alleging that the studio wanted him to “sign away my rights.”

Prior to seeing the film, Hansen slammed it as a “very dramatized version” of events and even purchased advertisements for his own true crime network to air before every single screening of Primetime. In contrast to Hansen’s opinion, we at IGN scored the film a glowing nine out of 10, calling it a “blast from the past with a sickly allure” that’s “as garish as its subject: Chris Hansen’s To Catch a Predator.”

Image Credits: Mike Pont/WireImage via Getty Images

items.title: Infinity Festival Returns to Los Angeles in November With a Focus on AI
items.description: Infinity Festival returns to the Audrey Irmas Pavilion in Los Angeles this November for its 9th edition, featuring panels and programming focused on how AI is reshaping the entertainment industry.
items.author: Michael Peyton
items.content:
Infinity Festival, an annual event celebrating the convergence of entertainment, technology, and creativity, is returning to Los Angeles this November for its 9th edition. From November 12-15, the festival will be taking over the Audrey Irmas Pavilion for “four days of ideas, experiences, screenings, demonstrations, and conversations about what comes next.”

In previous years, the festival has hosted guests like Avengers directors the Russo Brothers, Brie Larson, Jon Favreau, Project Hail Mary directors Phil Lord and Chris Miller, Jeff Bridges, and many more. This year, the festival promises to dive deep into AI, with panels focusing on its “growing role across the creative industries.” Instead of a standalone track, AI will be present through a broader program “spanning animation, gaming, sports tech, filmmaking, music, virtual production, and live entertainment.”

At the event, AI-focused programming will “explore the evolving tools and workflows behind animation and filmmaking, the growing crossover between gaming and entertainment, new technologies reshaping live sports and fan experiences, as well as advances in immersive production and live event design.”

Additionally, longtime partners like NVIDIA and HP will participate in the festival’s 2026 programming slate, which will feature “panels, keynotes, screenings, demonstrations, and exhibitions, with speakers and programming to be announced in the coming weeks.”

“The changes happening across entertainment and technology aren’t taking place in separate lanes anymore, and Infinity Festival is built for that reality,” said Mark Lieber, Founder and CEO of Infinity Festival. “We’re thrilled to have NVIDIA, HP, and Intel return as presenting sponsors as we bring together the creative and technology communities shaping where these industries go next.”

For more information about Infinity Festival, check out www.infinityfestival.com.

From November 12-15, the festival will be taking over the Audrey Irmas Pavilion for “four days of ideas, experiences, screenings, demonstrations, and conversations about what comes next.”

In previous years, the festival has hosted guests like Avengers directors the Russo Brothers, Brie Larson, Jon Favreau, Project Hail Mary directors Phil Lord and Chris Miller, Jeff Bridges, and many more. This year, the festival promises to dive deep into AI, with panels focusing on its “growing role across the creative industries.” Instead of a standalone track, AI will be present through a broader program “spanning animation, gaming, sports tech, filmmaking, music, virtual production, and live entertainment.”

At the event, AI-focused programming will “explore the evolving tools and workflows behind animation and filmmaking, the growing crossover between gaming and entertainment, new technologies reshaping live sports and fan experiences, as well as advances in immersive production and live event design.”

Additionally, longtime partners like NVIDIA and HP will participate in the festival’s 2026 programming slate, which will feature “panels, keynotes, screenings, demonstrations, and exhibitions, with speakers and programming to be announced in the coming weeks.”

“The changes happening across entertainment and technology aren’t taking place in separate lanes anymore, and Infinity Festival is built for that reality,” said Mark Lieber, Founder and CEO of Infinity Festival. “We’re thrilled to have NVIDIA, HP, and Intel return as presenting sponsors as we bring together the creative and technology communities shaping where these industries go next.”

For more information about Infinity Festival, check out www.infinityfestival.com.

items.title: Viral Resident Evil Stunt Footage Shows the Wild Way the 'Katamari Monster' Came to Life in Zach Cregger's Movie
items.description: With Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil movie now in theaters, staff who worked on the film are sharing behind-the-scenes footage of how it all came together, including a jaw-dropping look at the stunt team behind one of its monsters.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
With Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil movie now in theaters, staff who worked on the film are sharing behind-the-scenes footage of how it all came together, including a jaw-dropping look at the stunt team behind one of its monsters.

Warning: Spoilers for Resident Evil ahead!

Resident Evil is known for its wide variety of zombies, but some of the mutations we saw in Cregger’s version of events were brand-new and extremely gnarly. The main stalker monster of the film has been a hot topic of discussion within the games’ fanbase, with many affectionately dubbing it the ‘Katamari Monster.’

If you’ve seen the film and played the Katamari games, you’ll immediately understand why it’s been given this humorous moniker; its specific mutation includes some tentacle-like creatures that reach for other infected bodies and combine them into a mass of arms and legs that rolls around town, much like a Katamari.

Most viewers, myself included, figured this monster was a pure work of CGI. But astonishingly, this isn’t the case, as one of the stunt performers tasked with creating its movements proved in a now-viral Instagram post.

Jakub Hudlicky, a performer with Movement Production in the Czech Republic, published a series of videos showing himself and several other stuntpeople all strapped together with vests. Working together, the team made their way from one side of a soundstage to another, just like how the Katamari monster moved in Cregger’s film.

While the final product was, of course, modeled and put together using computer graphics, its movement was taken from these hard-working stunt performers, with Hudlicky explaining in a comment that the actual footage of them was “not in the final movie, but the movement kinda mimics how the CGI creature moves."

Hudlicky said the videos were filmed in July 2025, when he and the stunt team gathered together to figure out how the creature would actually locomote to chase Bryan around Raccoon City. Thanks to their performance, the Katamari monster rolls around like a group of actual human beings using its arms and legs, providing essential information to the CGI artists and animators responsible for creating it in the movie.

This is the latest insight from Cregger’s Resident Evil to go viral after the director admitted that its ending wasn’t actually the original conclusion he’d written for the film; instead, he described its final sequence as a “contingency plan” that he’d filmed to “keep the stakes all the way until the end.”

“It's like, ‘save him, save him.’ Whereas before it was just like ‘kill them all,’” he explained.

Resident Evil has been a major success, garnering mostly positive reviews and becoming the most successful film adaptation of Capcom’s flagship horror game franchise ever. IGN’s Tom Jorgensen scored the flick an eight out of 10, praising it for being “a simple and exciting survival horror story that benefits greatly from Zach Cregger’s sensibilities.

items.title: PlayStation's Newest Survey Sparks Community Pushback Against Sony's Plans to End Physical Game Discs
items.description: PlayStation has released a survey that any member of the public can fill out, as long as they’re an adult — and players are using the opportunity to push back on Sony’s plans to end the production of physical game discs.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
PlayStation has released a survey that any member of the public can fill out, as long as they’re an adult — and players are using the opportunity to push back on Sony’s plans to end the production of physical game discs.

PlayStation published the survey on September 25, just days after reports surfaced that the company had sent a different survey around to game developers.

This most recent open survey contains questions regarding customer satisfaction with their PlayStation 5 console, including aspects like PlayStation exclusive games, user interface, game performance, the ability to play online with others, the DualSense controller, as well as both PS5 exclusive games and the console’s overall library.

Players are also asked to list all the consoles they currently own, including those not under Sony’s umbrella, such as the Nintendo Switch, Gaming PCs, VR headsets, etc. At a few points during the survey, players are asked to elaborate on their choices, giving them the ability to offer direct feedback to PlayStation — and while none of these questions directly address physical media, there’s certainly room for players to bring up the topic on their own.

Many fans are hopeful that this is a sign PlayStation and Sony are showing some hesitation toward their plans to kill physical game discs starting January 2028, a choice that has been met with vitriol from just about every corner of the gaming community ever since it was first announced in July.

“I don't think they are ready for the responses, but this survey is a sign that they are at the very least aware that their public image has taken a helluva kicking lately,” one user wrote on Twitter/X.

“Filled it out. Respectfully told them they've been the worst all year lol,” another remarked.

Another player attached a screenshot of their written response in the survey, where they wrote, “To access this information, please insert the ‘my opinion’ disc into the disc drive, plus download the needed information from the internet.”

As previously mentioned, this survey comes hot on the heels of another survey that PlayStation reportedly sent out to game developers just a few days earlier. Speaking on the Broken Silicon Podcast, host Tom said it was “one of the biggest” surveys that developers had ever received from PlayStation, and similarly questioned if it didn’t signal some hesitation on Sony’s part regarding its choice to stop making game discs.

However, it’s worth noting that executives at the company have maintained their stance on the subject, with chief financial officer Lin Tao saying in a July investor Q&A that it is going to “cautiously move this forward” despite being well-aware of the public’s “strong views” on the topic.

items.title: GTA 6 Fans Are Already 3D Printing Items in the Game's $400 Collector's Edition
items.description: Fans of GTA 6 are already copying items in the game’s $400 collector’s edition and 3D-printing them for a far cheaper price.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Fans of GTA 6 are already copying items from the game’s $400 collector’s edition and 3D-printing them for a far cheaper price.

On September 24, Rockstar revealed a special, $400 collector’s edition for GTA 6… except it doesn’t actually come with the game. Despite putting up nearly half a rack, players won’t get the game itself; instead, it comes with a bunch of GTA 6-branded merchandise.

The bundle includes items like a cartoon alligator figure, stickers, pins, a hat, and a pair of Oakley sunglasses, which is probably where most of the cost is coming from. And while fans can’t exactly copy those, they are 3D printing copies of a at least one trinket in the collection.

One of the most viral examples of this is a recreation of the game’s Macca the Alligator mascot, which has been fully modeled and uploaded as a printable file online. And rather than paying $400, fans can simply support its creator by paying what they want.

Reactions to this workaround have been extremely divided; some fans are giving the copycat props for their creative solution to a pricey problem, while others are rallying against them, saying that making a 3D copy completely defeats the purpose of buying a rare item.

“Why would you print it if it already lost its main and only purpose, which is rarity?” one user asked on X/Twitter.

Pra quem desacreditou… a primeira parte do jacaré baitola já foi… só imprimir agr o rabo e a base kkkkkk#gtavı pic.twitter.com/iTzsQoHixt

— Santiago 🕊️ (@JSantiag0rj) September 25, 2026

“Dude, I’m all for criticizing the price, but this is just f**king stupid,” another argued.

“I imagined this would happen, but not so soon... That said, I want one,” another commenter admitted.

“This is the coolest thing! I only wanted this [figure], but I wasn’t about to drop $400 to get it,” another wrote.

The GTA 6 collector’s edition has sparked a viral debate within the broader gaming community, with many comparing it to the Red Dead Redemption 2 collector’s edition, which was far cheaper and had comparatively cooler, more game-specific items. It only cost $100, and even came with some in-game goodies like a physical version of the game’s map.

The $400 price tag for GTA 6's collector's edition without an actual game to show for it is rubbing salt in the wound for gamers who are mourning the lack of a true physical disc. The ‘physical’ version of GTA 6 is in name only; it’ll get a case, but only a downloadable code inside. And while this is likely part of Rockstar’s plans to stop early leaks, players can’t help but point to Sony’s plans to end the production of physical game discs completely by January 2028.

items.title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation Will Be Easier to Platinum Than Rebirth
items.description: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is still a few months away, but it seems like it's at least going to be easier to get the Platinum trophy than it was in Rebirth.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is still a few months away, but it seems like it's at least going to be easier to get the Platinum trophy than it was in Rebirth.

Speaking to Anime News Network, game director Naoki Hamaguchi was asked why only 2.6% of PS5 players had the Platinum trophy for Rebirth, specifically citing the post-game VR boss gauntlets and the perfect play they required. And while Hamaguchi stands by the design decisions, he does explain why the trophy was so out of reach.

"For Rebirth's platinum trophy — well, for Rebirth in general — there's so much to do. There's so much content. We wanted to make people go through all this content and perfect it. It's kind of by design that that would make it difficult." Despite that difficulty, Hamaguchi doesn't regret making it that way, saying, "So, I don't want to call it a mistake in judgment or anything, but we also didn't expect so many people to want the platinum trophy. I think that was what we underestimated here. Battle director Teruki Endo also saw [the fan reaction] and was like, 'Oh, no! I feel bad — I have regrets.'"

While the Final Fantasy 7 Revelation Platinum trophy will probably still be huge in scope, it should at least be a little bit easier to get, especially where the superbosses are concerned. "In comparison, for Revelation, the platinum trophy will be easier to get," Hamaguchi says. "In terms of how difficult it will be, we're expecting twenty percent of players or maybe even more than that to be able to obtain it." Specifically, he mentioned that, "It's not just about the amount of battles that there are, but the battles themselves that are going to be enjoyable. I think that's one thing that we've learned from Rebirth: to make the battles themselves enjoyable rather than just challenging."

It sounds like the optional bosses aren't going to be quite as much of a grind as they were in Rebirth, though hopefully there is still some challenge there.

We won't have to wait too much longer to see how these post-game battles play out. Final Fantasy Revelation comes out on February 8, 2027 for Xbox Series X, PlayStation 5, PC and Nintendo Switch 2. And while you will need to download it to play, even if you buy it on a disc, you can at least expect the game to last for more than 100 hours.
